svvoicechanger.ai.train.guide:
# What to record
10-30 minutes of one person talking. More does not help: 15 clean minutes beat an hour with noise.
Talk normally and vary it: calm, loud, asking, laughing. Talking works better than singing.
# How to record
A quiet room, no music, echo or other voices. Keep the mic close but not clipping: if it crackles, move back.
Any recorder will do, even a phone's. Files in wav, mp3, flac or ogg, any length, as many as you like.
# Someone else's voice
Only with that person's consent. A recording from a video works too once the music and other people are cut out.
# Then
Put the files in the voice's folder, press Check recordings, then Train.

svvoicechanger.ai.where.rvc:
# Where to get voices
Ready-made RVC models are on Hugging Face (search for "RVC") and on model catalogue sites. You need the .pth file and, if there is one, the .index.
# How to add one
Press Add a voice below: the voices folder opens. Drop the .pth and .index there, or the downloaded .zip without unpacking it. In a few seconds the voice shows up in the gallery and is picked; nothing to press.
# What is fine
Your own voices, original characters, and people who agreed to it. Do not pass yourself off as real people.

svvoicechanger.ai.help.voice_engine:
# What it is
A free engine that changes your voice on your own PC, live, about 0.2 s behind. It wants an NVIDIA RTX 20xx card or newer; without one it runs on the CPU, slowly. Windows only for now.
# Install
1. Press Install engine in this tab and agree. The mod downloads the engine, Python and the packages it needs, about 3.5 GB. Nothing to install by hand.
2. Wait: the progress shows under the buttons. The first start after installing fetches about 370 MB more and reads "starting" meanwhile.
3. The engine starts by itself while the AI voice is on and closes with the game.
# Voices
Press Voices folder and put RVC models there (.pth, and an added_... .index if there is one). Then press Refresh and pick a Model.
# In game
1. At the top, set "Voice: AI" and the engine to Auto or Voice Engine.
2. Pitch: +12 when a male voice speaks into a female model, -12 the other way.
3. Chunk: raise it if the voice stutters.
4. Turn on Self Listen and say something.
# Removing it
Remove engine deletes everything that was installed. Your voices are in the game folder (voice-changer\voices) and stay.
# If it does not work
The install line shows which step failed; the full log is in the engine folder, under logs.
A VPN should not get in the way: the mod talks to the engine directly, past any proxy. If a TUN-mode VPN still breaks local connections, add 127.0.0.1 to its exclusions.

svvoicechanger.ai.install.consent:
# What is downloaded
The Voice Changer Engine (this mod's engine), Python 3.12 and the neural network packages for your graphics card (%2$s): about %3$s GB, plus about 370 MB on the first start.
# From where
The engine from the mod author's GitHub, the uv installer from astral-sh's GitHub, Python and the packages from the official Python and PyTorch servers, models from Hugging Face. Every file the mod downloads is checked against a checksum.
# Where to
%1$s
Everything stays in that folder: nothing is installed system-wide and nothing starts with Windows.
# How it runs
The engine starts only while the AI voice is on and the game is open, and closes with the game. It runs on your PC only; your voice is not sent anywhere.
# Removing it
Any time, with Remove engine in this tab, or by deleting the folder.

svvoicechanger.ai.help.w_okada:
# What it is
w-okada's Voice Changer: a free program for RVC models, live. The mod talks to the open-source version 1.5 (MMVCServerSIO); the newer VCClient 2.x is closed source and has not been tried with the mod.
# Install
1. Download MMVCServerSIO 1.5 for your graphics card from w-okada's GitHub page and unpack it.
2. Start it. A page opens in your browser; the server listens on port 18888.
3. Load an RVC model into any slot on that page.
# In game
1. At the top, set "Voice: AI" and the engine to Auto or w-okada.
2. Below, open w-okada, check the address 127.0.0.1:18888 and press Refresh.
3. Your slots appear under Model; pick one.
4. Pitch: +12 or -12 to switch between a male and a female voice. Chunk: raise it if the voice stutters.
No virtual audio cable is needed: the mod sends your microphone to w-okada and the answer straight into voice chat.
# If it does not work
"not running": w-okada is closed, uses another port, or is VCClient 2.x.
w-okada can run on a second PC on your home network: enter its address, for example 192.168.1.20:18888.
A VPN should not get in the way: the mod talks to w-okada directly, past any proxy.
svvoicechanger.ai.help.elevenlabs:
# What it is
ElevenLabs' cloud voices with your own key. The best quality, but paid: about $0.12 per minute of speech, with a few free credits a month. Not live: others hear you about a second after you stop talking or let go of the key.
# Key
1. Sign up at elevenlabs.io.
2. Press Get a key, create an API key and copy it.
3. Press Paste key from clipboard. The key stays on this PC and is never shown on screen.
# Voice
1. Press "Voice: pick one" and choose a voice from your ElevenLabs list.
2. To add more, open Voice library, add a voice to your list and press Refresh here.
3. At the top, set "Voice: AI" and the engine to Auto or ElevenLabs.
# Settings
Stability: higher is steadier, lower more expressive. Similarity: how closely to stick to the voice. Style: usually 0. Remove noise cleans room noise out first.
# If it does not work
ElevenLabs is not available from some countries, Russia among them, so you need a VPN. If the VPN works as a Windows system proxy, the mod uses it by itself.
"key rejected": copy the key again. "out of credits": wait for the next month or change the plan.

svvoicechanger.slider.pitch.desc: Moves the perceived voice height up or down.
svvoicechanger.slider.formant.desc: Changes vocal character without behaving exactly like pitch.
svvoicechanger.slider.low_eq.desc: Bass amount. Raise for fuller voices, lower for radio or child voices.
svvoicechanger.slider.mid_eq.desc: Body and intelligibility of the voice. Useful for radio-style presence.
svvoicechanger.slider.high_eq.desc: Brightness and air. Too much can make the voice sharp or harsh.
svvoicechanger.slider.distortion.desc: Adds grit and saturation. Use lightly unless you want monster tones.
svvoicechanger.slider.bit_crush.desc: Reduces the voice to fewer bits (16, 8, 3...). Turn right for a crunchier, retro lo-fi sound. Full left = clean.
svvoicechanger.slider.noise.desc: Adds hiss texture. Best for radio, almost always low for normal voices.
svvoicechanger.slider.robot_mix.desc: Metallic modulation layer for robotic or synthetic voices.
svvoicechanger.slider.robot_frequency.de: Carrier frequency of the robot layer. Higher is thinner and buzzier.
svvoicechanger.slider.echo_mix.desc: Amount of cave or room tail blended into the processed voice.
svvoicechanger.slider.echo_feedback.desc: Length of the tail. Higher values feel larger and more haunted.
svvoicechanger.slider.tremolo_depth.desc: How strongly the voice volume wobbles over time.
svvoicechanger.slider.autotune_mix.desc: How much the auto-tuned voice replaces your natural pitch. 0 disables autotune.
How fast the pitch snaps to the chosen note. Higher values give the classic robotic T-Pain effect.
svvoicechanger.slider.autotune_key.desc: Root note of the scale used for autotune snapping.

svvoicechanger.param.mix.desc: How much of the processed voice replaces your original microphone.
svvoicechanger.param.gain.desc: Output loudness after the whole chain. The limiter stops it from clipping.
svvoicechanger.param.pitch.desc: Moves the note of your voice up or down, in semitones. Does not change your body size: that is Formant.
svvoicechanger.param.formant.desc: How big the speaker sounds. Below 100% is a bigger head and chest, above 100% is smaller. Raise Pitch without raising this and you sound like a woman; raise both and you sound like a chipmunk.
svvoicechanger.param.voiceMatch.desc: How much the preset aims at a fixed target voice instead of just multiplying your pitch. At 100% the voice lands the same whoever is speaking, so a high voice does not become a chipmunk. Turn it down to treat Pitch as a plain multiplier.
svvoicechanger.param.growl.desc: Adds an octave below your voice for chest weight. The core of the Batman, Titan and Demon voices.
svvoicechanger.param.lowEq.desc: Low frequencies. Raise for a fuller voice, lower for a thinner or radio voice.
svvoicechanger.param.midEq.desc: Body and clarity. Raising it pushes the voice forward and makes it easier to understand.
svvoicechanger.param.highEq.desc: Brightness and air. Too much sounds sharp; the de-esser keeps it from hissing.
svvoicechanger.param.radio.desc: Narrows the voice to a telephone or walkie-talkie band.
svvoicechanger.param.gate.desc: Mutes the microphone between words so fans, keyboards and room noise are not sent. Raise it in a noisy room; lower it if quiet speech gets cut off.
svvoicechanger.param.deEss.desc: Softens harsh S sounds. Useful whenever the pitch is raised.
svvoicechanger.param.distortion.desc: Adds grit and saturation. A little for character, a lot for monsters.
svvoicechanger.param.bitDepth.desc: Reduces the voice to fewer bits for a retro, lo-fi sound. 16 bit is clean.
svvoicechanger.param.noise.desc: Adds carrier hiss. Made for the Radio voice; it stays silent when you are not speaking.
svvoicechanger.param.robotMix.desc: Metallic ring-modulated layer for robotic or synthetic voices.
svvoicechanger.param.robotFrequency.desc: Carrier frequency of the robot layer. Higher is thinner and buzzier.
svvoicechanger.param.tremoloDepth.desc: How strongly the volume wobbles over time.
svvoicechanger.param.reverbMix.desc: How much room tail is mixed into the voice.
svvoicechanger.param.reverbSize.desc: From a small booth to a large hall.
svvoicechanger.param.reverbDecay.desc: How long the tail rings on. Higher feels larger and more haunted.
svvoicechanger.param.autotuneMix.desc: Pulls your pitch toward the nearest note of the chosen scale. 0% is off.
svvoicechanger.param.autotuneStrength.de: How fast the pitch snaps to the note. Low glides between notes, high gives the classic robotic effect.
svvoicechanger.param.autotuneKey.desc: Root note of the scale autotune snaps to.
svvoicechanger.param.autotuneScale.desc: Which notes the voice is allowed to snap to.
